should contact the Community Services Department via email at

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the Recreation
Commission on any item of interest that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the
Recreation Commission. Pursuant to state law, the Recreation Commission may not discuss or

Chair reserves the right to place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to
follow up on such items.

MINUTES
  REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE SAN MARINO RECREATION COMMISSION
  MONDAY, MAY 8, 2023 AT 6:00 P.M.
  BARTH ROOM, CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY

CALL TO ORDER: Chairperson Yen called the regular meeting to order at 6:03 p.m. in the Barth
Room, located at 1890 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California 91108.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Scarlett Yen led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL:  PRESENT: Commissioner Tsai, Commissioner Wu, Vice Chairperson Solan,
  and Chairperson Yen

  ABSENT: Commissioner Tam

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

COMMISSIONER REPORTS

Chairperson Yen acknowledged Commissioner Wu for speaking in support of the Recreation
Division’s budget request at the last City Council meeting. He also acknowledged that May is AAPI
Heritage Month.

NEW BUSINESS

1. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

Commissioner Wu moved, seconded by Commissioner Tsai, to approve the minutes from March
13, 2023 and April 18, 2023.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Commissioner Tsai, Commissioner Wu, Vice Chairperson Solan, and Chairperson
  Yen
NOES:  None
ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  Commissioner Tam

MAY 8, 2023  PAGE 2 OF 4

2. DIRECTOR AND RECREATION MANAGER REPORT

Director Johnson and Recreation Manager Covarrubias presented the staff report.

Vice Chairperson Solan explained that the abbreviation “SMCC” for the new Community Center
may cause confusion among community members since there are other locations in the City with
the same abbreviation. Director Johnson clarified that staff will be using the abbreviation “CC” to
avoid any confusion.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

3. PREVIEW OF SUMMER PROGRAMMING

Recreation Manager Covarrubias presented the staff report.

Chairperson Yen asked if CivicRec has been upgraded or changed in the last month. Director
Johnson responded that it is the same software; the Department transitioned to CivicRec about 2
years ago. Recreation Manager Covarrubias shared that minimal complaints or glitches have been
reported since summer registration began last week.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

4. REVIEW AND DISCUSS DRAFT FACILITY USE AND RENTAL GUIDELINES
  DOCUMENT

Director Johnson presented the staff report.

Chairperson Yen inquired if the application will be made available online. Director Johnson
responded that the application will be available online, but submission of an application does not
mean it has been approved; a meeting with staff will still need to occur. Recreation Manager
Covarrubias responded that if potential renters are unable to come see the facility, they will be
offered a soft hold and given 5 business days to tour the facility; if the potential renter does not
come in 5 days, the date will be given to the next person who requested that date. Vice Chairperson
Solan asked if potential renters are required to complete a walk through of the facility before
approval of their application. Recreation Manager Covarrubias responded that a walk through with
the facilities coordinator is required before a confirmation.

Chairperson Yen noted that there’s a soft reservation process and an application process which may
cause double bookings and confusion among renters; he recommended staff consider removing the
soft reservation guidelines and have it be more of an informal protocol. Commissioner Wu
recommended providing clarity on what happens when a soft reservation and application are
received at the same time. Commissioner Tsai recommended that a clause be added to Section 5.5.1
saying that an application may be denied if there’s a soft reservation in place. Vice Chairperson Solan
recommended adding a reference under the application details to the soft reservation section and
 RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
MAY 8, 2023  PAGE 3 OF 4

vice versa so potential renters are aware of both options. Chairperson Yen recommended adding
Section 5.3.5 to make soft reservations part of the applications procedures as a courtesy to new
renters. Director Johnson shared that some of these details on both processes can be addressed
and clarified on the website. The Commission agreed to add strong clarifying information about Soft
Reservations and the Formal Application on the website.

Commissioner Tsai recommended making the cost of security clear on the website so it is not a
“hidden” cost that renters find out about late in the application process. Director Johnson shared
that she has already spoken with staff about how critical the website is going to be to communicate
information that renters will need to make their decisions. Chairperson Yen shared that since there
are different levels of security, it will be a good idea to make the security costs available. He also
suggested a master services agreement where you have multiple vendors so staff have the ability to
choose from a few in case one vendor is busy. Commissioner Tsai pointed out that some renters
may try to sneak alcohol in if security costs are too high and run the risk of getting a small slap on
the wrist. Recreation Manager Covarrubias clarified that there is language in the document saying
that the City can terminate the event at any time.

Chairperson Yen asked what the difference is between a liquor license and a beer and wine license,
and will both be covered by full liquor liability insurance. Director Johnson responded that the City’s
insurance provider will provide clarity on this. Chairperson Yen also pointed out that Section 10.2.15
states that renters cannot bring their own alcohol. Recreation Manager Covarrubias explained that
there have been instances in the past where renters have asked to bring in alcohol, but the current
document states that is not allowed; he added that the City’s insurance provider will provide clarity.
Commissioner Tsai recommended that if staff have a hard time renting the facility to smaller groups
over the alcohol provisions, staff may want to consider more flexible rules. Recreation Manager
Covarrubias explained that it becomes hard for staff to monitor and gauge how many drinks
everyone has had.

Commissioner Wu expressed concern over Section 10.2.12 which states that alcohol can be served
or consumed in the parking lot with approval from the City. He asked if other cities have similar
provisions given the increase in liability. Recreation Manager Covarrubias explained that the reason
why that was included is because food trucks may use the parking lot or large scale events might
have a beer garden; it is included as an option for potential renters.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

Commissioner Tsai moved, seconded by Commissioner Wu, to support staff’s recommended
changes to the Facility Use and Rental Guidelines and the submittal of the document to City
leadership for final approval.
